subject: Logic
title: Descartes' Evil Demon
description: A short lesson to help you apply Descartes' Evil Demon.

hook.text: What if an all-powerful demon is deceiving you about everything—math, senses, even your own body?

buildup.text: Descartes proposed this in 1641 as the ultimate test of doubt. What can survive even demon-level deception?

discovery.text: His answer: I think, therefore I am. Even a demon can't fake the fact that something is doing the thinking.

twist.text: It doesn't prove the world exists—only that a thinking subject exists. Everything else remains uncertain.

climax.text: The experiment didn't aim to cause paranoia. It aimed to find one unshakeable foundation for knowledge.

quiz.question: What did Descartes conclude survives even total deception?
